    Answers to our
    frequently asked

    An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party organization that legally employs workers on behalf of another company. The EOR handles all employment-related responsibilities, such as payroll, taxes, benefits, compliance, and HR administration, while the client company manages the employee’s day-to-day work and performance.

    Companies use an EOR to simplify hiring and employment in locations where they don’t have a legal entity or HR infrastructure. An EOR helps organizations:

    • Hire talent quickly without setting up a local entity
    • Reduce compliance and payroll risks
    • Expand into new markets cost-effectively
    • Manage contractors transitioning to full-time roles
    • Offload administrative HR tasks so they can focus on core operations

    The EOR becomes the legal employer of the worker, while your company directs the employee’s actual work. In practice:

    • You choose and manage the talent
    • The EOR issues employment contracts aligned with local laws
    • The EOR runs payroll, handles visas and work permits, provides benefits, and ensures compliance
    • Both parties coordinate on HR matters like onboarding, performance issues, and offboarding
      This shared-responsibility model lets businesses stay compliant without sacrificing control over daily operations.

    No. While EORs are commonly used for international hiring, they’re equally valuable for domestic scenarios. Companies may use an EOR to ensure compliance when operating in jurisdictions with complex employment laws or when facing visa quota limitations in the UAE. Essentially, an EOR is useful anywhere an organization wants to hire without taking on full administrative and legal employer obligations.

title: Employer of Record (EOR) in Dubai & Abudhabi, UAE
content:
Employer of Record (EOR) Services in the UAE

Hire Employees in Dubai & Abu Dhabi Without Setting Up a Company

Employer of Record UAE enables foreign companies to hire employees legally without establishing a local entity. We handle payroll processing, employment contracts, work visas, MOHRE compliance, and HR administration, while you maintain full control over your team’s daily operations and performance. Expand into Dubai and the wider UAE market quickly, compliantly, and without unnecessary setup costs or delays.

Contact Us

UAE Employer of Record Services
“licensed, local, compliant”

Connect Resources is proud to be one of the limited number of companies licensed to offer Employer of Record services in the UAE.

As a 100% Emirati-owned company, we offer:

Faster visa and work permit processing

Strong local authority relationships

Guaranteed alignment with UAE labour regulations

Our EOR solutions are designed for international companies, regional businesses, and growing teams that need speed, compliance, and flexibility when hiring in the UAE.

Who our Employer of Record Services are for?

Contact Us

Our Employer of Record UAE solution is ideal if you:

Want to hire employees in the UAE without forming a legal entity

Are relocating staff to Dubai or Abu Dhabi

Need fast, compliant onboarding and payroll

Want to test the UAE market before incorporation

Prefer to avoid long-term HR, payroll, and legal overhead

This solution may not be suitable if:

You already have a registered UAE entity

You plan to hire a large permanent workforce immediately

You want to manage payroll and compliance fully in-house

Contact Us

What’s included in our UAE
Employer of Record Services?

Our end-to-end EOR services typically include:

UAE-compliant employment contracts

Visa and work permit processing

Payroll processing and payslips

Statutory tax and social contributions

Mandatory employee benefits

Labour law compliance and reporting

Onboarding and offboarding support

HR and employment advisory

Where applicable, we also support employee relocation and immigration services.

How Employer of Record Services work in the UAE?

Our EOR process is simple, structured, and compliant:

Role & compensation confirmation

You select the employee and define salary, benefits, and role requirements.

Employment & visa setup

We issue a compliant UAE employment contract and process visas and work permits.

Onboarding & payroll activation

The employee is onboarded, payroll is set up, and benefits are enrolled.

Ongoing HR & compliance management

We manage payroll, labour law compliance, renewals, and terminations.

You focus on performance and growth we handle the legal employment framework.

Why choose Connect Resources for EOR Services in the UAE?

Licensed by MOHRE

We are officially licensed by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE), ensuring 100% compliance with UAE labour laws.

100% Emirati-Owned

Our local ownership enables faster processing, stronger regulatory alignment, and smoother government interactions.

End-to-End Workforce Solutions

Beyond EOR, we support recruitment, immigration, HR outsourcing, payroll, and legal advisory all under one roof.

Flexible & Scalable

Hire one employee or scale a full team across Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and the wider UAE without changing your structure.

Key benefits of using an Employer of Record in the UAE?

Rapid market entry

Hire employees in the UAE without setting up a company.

Reduced compliance risk

Stay aligned with local labour laws and employment regulations.

Simplified payroll & benefits

Accurate salary processing and statutory benefit administration.

Cost efficiency

Avoid entity setup, legal retainers, and internal HR overhead.

Focus on growth

We manage employment and you focus on business results.

Employer of Record vs Setting Up a UAE Entity

Setting up a UAE entity involves:

Licensing and registration

Payroll and tax registration

Ongoing compliance obligations

Legal and HR overhead

An Employer of Record allows you to:

Hire legally without incorporation

Move faster with lower upfront costs

Transition to an entity later if needed

Many companies use EOR as a market-entry or expansion phase before formal incorporation.

Contact Us

Hiring across Dubai, Abu Dhabi & the UAE

With Connect Resources, you can hire employees across:

Dubai

Abu Dhabi

Other UAE Emirates

Our local presence and regulatory expertise ensure your workforce is compliant wherever your team is based.

CONTACT US NOW

Other Services

Other Workforce Solutions We Offer

Staff Outsourcing

Ideal for project-based, contract, or flexible workforce needs where EOR may not be required.

Learn More

Payroll Outsourcing

Best for companies that already have a UAE entity and need compliant payroll support.

Learn More

PRO Services

Government documentation, company formation support, visa processing, and labour compliance handled end-to-end.

Learn More

FAQs

Find answers to frequently asked questions about Employer of Record services (EOR) in the UAE.

Contact Us

An Employer of Record (UAE) is an agency that offers legal services that include employing and managing staff for international businesses. This includes taking responsibility for duties such as adherence to regulations, payroll, taxation, and employee benefits.

A company can use an EOR for different reasons. These include, save time and money on administrative tasks, reduce legal and financial risks associated with international hiring, and gain access to a larger pool of talent. Likewise, an EOR can provide compliance support, employee onboarding services, payroll processing, and other related services.

When a company hires an EOR, they start a multilateral business relationship with the EOR and the employees. The business and the employees remain in direct contact, also, the business is responsible for overseeing and assigning tasks and projects. Likewise, they must monitor employee performance and other duties.

No, an Employer of Record (EOR) is not only for international expansion. An EOR can be used for a variety of purposes, including but not limited to:

  • Reducing the administrative burden of onboarding and managing employees
  • Streamlining payroll and human resource processes
  • Complying with local labor laws
  • Managing employee contracts and benefits
  • Securing workers’ compensation insurance
  • Reducing risk and liability associated with hiring employees.

The benefits of using an EOR include:

  • Time saving.
  • More precision.
  • Up-to-date records.
  • Less international regulatory risks.
  • Less overhead costs.
  • Use of technology and much more.

title: EOR vs. Staffing Agency: Key Differences and When to Use Each

Employer of Record vs Staffing Agency: What’s the Difference and When to Use Each

When expanding a workforce or hiring across borders, companies often compare two very different options: an Employer of Record and a staffing agency. While both support hiring, they solve fundamentally different problems.

Understanding the difference between an employer of record and a staffing agency is critical for compliance, cost control, and long-term workforce planning especially when hiring internationally.

This guide explains the employer of record vs staffing agency in clear, practical terms so you can choose the right model for your hiring goals.

The simplest way to understand employer of record vs staffing agency is this:

  • An Employer of Record is an employment solution.
  • A staffing agency is a recruitment solution.

What an Employer of Record Does

An Employer of Record (EOR) becomes the legal employer of a worker on behalf of your company. This allows businesses to hire employees in countries where they do not have a legal entity.

In an EOR arrangement, the provider handles employment contracts, payroll processing, statutory taxes, benefits administration, and compliance with local labor laws. Your company continues to manage the employee’s day-to-day work, performance, and reporting, but the legal employment responsibility sits with the EOR.

This model is commonly used for international hiring, market entry, and long-term remote employment.

Contact Us

What a Staffing Agency Does

A staffing agency focuses primarily on sourcing and placing talent.

Staffing agencies recruit, screen, and present candidates for temporary, contract, or permanent roles. In most cases, once the candidate is hired, the staffing agency’s role ends. Legal employment responsibility typically transfers to your company unless the agency directly employs the worker for a temporary assignment.

Staffing agencies are especially valuable when speed of hiring, access to niche talent, or short-term workforce flexibility is the main objective.

Contact Us Now

Employer of Record vs Staffing Agency: Key Differences

Area Employer of Record (EOR) Staffing Agency
Primary role Employment and compliance Recruitment and placement
Legal employer EOR is the legal employer Usually the hiring company
Local entity required No Yes (in most cases)
Compliance ownership Managed through the EOR Largely remains with the company
Recruitment Not typically included Core service
Employment duration Long-term, ongoing roles Short-term, temp, or permanent placements
Geographic scope Global hiring without entities Typically local or regional
Post-hire involvement Ongoing (payroll, compliance, HR admin) Often ends after placement

This table highlights why eor vs staffing agency is not a like-for-like comparison.

Control and Management of Workers

With an Employer of Record, your company manages the employee’s daily work, goals, and performance just as it would with a direct hire. The difference is that the EOR handles the legal employment layer in the background.

With a staffing agency, the level of control depends on the arrangement. For permanent hires, control shifts entirely to your company after placement. For temporary or agency-employed workers, control may be shared, which can introduce co-employment considerations in some jurisdictions.

Compliance and Risk Considerations (Why This Matters)

Compliance is one of the most important and most misunderstood aspects of employer of record vs staffing agency.

An EOR is specifically designed to manage employment compliance, particularly across borders. This includes local labor laws, payroll regulations, statutory benefits, and termination rules.

Staffing agencies, by contrast, are not compliance outsourcing partners. While they must follow fair recruitment practices, your company typically remains responsible for employment law compliance once the worker is hired.

For companies hiring internationally or in unfamiliar jurisdictions, this difference can materially affect risk exposure.

Cost Structure: How the Models Differ

Cost comparisons between EORs and staffing agencies depend heavily on context, but the pricing logic is different.

EORs usually charge a recurring monthly fee per employee, covering employment administration, compliance, and payroll services. This creates predictable ongoing costs, particularly for long-term roles.

Staffing agencies often charge a one-time placement fee, commonly calculated as a percentage of the employee’s annual salary. For temporary staffing, agencies may apply markups to hourly or daily rates. These costs can appear lower upfront but may add up for long-term or repeat hiring.

The right choice depends less on headline cost and more on duration, compliance complexity, and internal HR capacity.

Which Is Faster?

Staffing agencies typically offer the fastest route to identifying candidates, especially for urgent or hard-to-fill roles. Their existing talent pools and recruitment expertise can significantly reduce time-to-hire.

An Employer of Record may not accelerate candidate sourcing, but it can dramatically reduce time-to-employment in new countries by removing the need to set up a legal entity. For global expansion, this often outweighs recruitment speed alone.

When an Employer of Record Is the Better Fit

An Employer of Record is usually the right choice when:

  • you need to hire employees in countries where you don’t have a legal entity
  • the roles are long-term and core to the business
  • employment compliance and risk reduction are priorities
  • you want a scalable, repeatable global hiring model

Hiring internationally without a local entity, book a FREE Consultation

When a Staffing Agency Makes More Sense

A staffing agency is usually the better choice when:

  • you need help finding candidates quickly
  • roles are short-term, seasonal, or project-based
  • you want to outsource recruitment but retain employment responsibility
  • hiring is local and entity setup is not a constraint

Need candidates for short-term projects locally, Find Talent Today

Can Companies Use Both? Yes and Many Do

In practice, many organizations use both models together. A staffing agency may be used to source candidates, while an Employer of Record is used to employ them compliantly in countries where no entity exists.

What matters is understanding that staffing employer of record is not a single solution it’s a combination of two distinct services with different purposes.

Final Thoughts: Employer of Record vs Staffing Agency Is About Intent

The decision between the employer of record vs staffing agency depends on what problem you’re trying to solve.

If the challenge is how to employ someone compliantly, especially across borders, an EOR is the appropriate model. If the challenge is how to find talent quickly, a staffing agency may be the better tool.

Understanding the difference helps avoid unnecessary risk, duplicated costs, and restructuring later.

title: Employer of Record (EOR) Hub
content:
Employer of Record (EOR)

Meaning, How It Works, Costs, Risks, and When to Use It

An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party organization that legally employs workers on behalf of another company. It enables businesses to hire employees in countries where they do not have a local legal entity, while remaining compliant with local labor, tax, and employment regulations.

Get Started

Get a Free Consultation

Reach out to us and let our experts guide you toward success!

    I'm interested in

    50,000+

    Employees on managed
    payroll

    Since 2016

    UAE payroll
    specialists

    100%

    On-time WPS accuracy
    SLA

    0

    MOHRE penalties for our
    clients

    Employer of Record availability by country

    Employer of Record solutions are widely used in regions with complex employment regulations or where companies want to test the market before committing to entity setup.

    UAE
    Saudi Arabia
    Qatar
    Oman
    Kuwait
    Jordan
    Egypt
    Lebanon

    Country specific rules, costs, and timelines vary and should always be reviewed individually.

    What is an Employer of Record?

    The Employer of Record definition refers to an organization that assumes the legal responsibility of employing workers on behalf of a client company. In an EOR arrangement:

    • The employee signs a locally compliant employment contract with the EOR
    • The EOR manages payroll, tax withholding, statutory benefits, and labor law compliance
    • The client company retains full operational control over day-to-day work and performance

    The client company retains operational control over the employee's daily work, performance, and team integration, while the EOR handles legal employment, payroll, and compliance obligations.

    Book a Consultation

    How does an Employer of Record (EOR) Work?

    An Employer of Record follows a clear and structured employment model.

    Hire full-time employees in any of 150+ countries

    Pay in multiple currencies without conversion headache

    Offer competitive, locally compliant benefits

    Stay 100% compliant without setting up local entities

    Get Started in a Few Simple Steps

    Global Hiring, Integrated with Your Existing HR Platform

    Expanding your workforce globally doesn't have to mean changing the way you work. Connect Resources integrates seamlessly with your existing HR, payroll, and workforce management systems, making it easy to hire, onboard, and manage employees across multiple countries from one centralized process.

    Start Hiring Globally

    Tell Us Where You Want to Hire

    Share your hiring requirements, target countries, and employee details. Our experts recommend the most compliant hiring approach for each location.

    We Handle Employment & Compliance

    We become the legal Employer of Record, managing employment contracts, onboarding, payroll, taxes, benefits, and statutory compliance while you manage the employee's day-to-day work.

    Connect with Your Existing Systems

    Our team works with your HR and payroll workflows to ensure smooth data sharing, employee management, and reporting with minimal disruption.

    Grow with Confidence

    Scale your global workforce quickly while we continue managing payroll, compliance, renewals, employee support, and local employment requirements in every country.

    Ready to Hire Internationally?

    Talk to an EOR Expert

    Why Companies Use an Employer of Record

    Organizations typically choose Employer of Record services when speed, compliance, and flexibility are critical.

    Faster global hiring

    An EOR enables companies to hire internationally in days instead of months—ideal for testing new markets
    or responding quickly to talent needs.

    Reduced compliance risk

    Employment laws vary widely by country. An EOR remains responsible for compliance with payroll, tax, benefits,
    termination rules, and statutory reporting.

    No local entity required

    Setting up a legal entity is costly and time-consuming. An EOR allows companies to hire
    without long-term legal commitments.

    Scalable hiring model

    Employer of Record arrangements work for hiring a single employee or scaling teams across multiple countries
    without duplicating HR infrastructure.

    Employer of Record Costs: What Companies Should Expect

    • Flat monthly fee per employee
    • Percentage of gross payroll
    • Hybrid pricing (base fee + variable costs)

    Employer of Record pricing varies by provider and country, but most EORs follow one of these models:

    Costs are influenced by:

    • Country of employment
    • Local statutory benefits and social contributions
    • Payroll complexity
    • Visa or work permit support (if applicable)

    While EOR may appear more expensive than local payroll on paper, it often replaces:

    • Entity setup costs
    • Local legal retainers
    • HR and compliance overhead
    • Compliance and reporting overhead

    For many companies, EOR is more cost-effective in the short to medium term.

    BUSINESS IMPACT DELIVERED WITH CONNECT RESOURCES

    Helping Businesses Expand Faster, Reduce Risk, and Scale Globally

    Connect Resources simplifies global employment by combining EOR services with in-house immigration, HR, and payroll expertise—so you can hire internationally with confidence.

    Hire Across 150+
    Countries

    Expand into new markets without setting up local legal entities—hire full-time employees compliantly
    in the countries that matter to your business.

    Faster Global
    Onboarding

    Onboard international employees quickly with compliant contracts, payroll setup, and local benefits
    aligned to each market.

    100% Local
    Compliance

    Stay compliant with local labor laws, tax obligations, and statutory reporting in every country
    where you hire through our EOR model.

    Simplified Global Payroll

    Pay employees in multiple currencies through a single monthly invoice—without conversion headaches or fragmented payroll systems.

Two Proven Ways to Stay Compliant (and Save Money)

Option 1

Lower your target with smart outsourcing

If your company employs fewer than 20 people, your Emiratization quota may not apply. We help you structure your workforce through our licensed Employer of Record (EOR) services, allowing you to stay below the threshold, without cutting staff or slowing growth.

Contact us today

Find top local talent
quickly

Prefer to build your own internal Emirati team? We’ve got you covered. Our talent network includes thousands of pre-screened Emiratis, from fresh graduates to senior executives. We can place qualified candidates with you in less than 48 hours, so you stay compliant and competitive.

Not sure how Emiratisation targets affect your business? This FAQ breaks down the essentials so you know exactly what’s required, and how to stay one step ahead.

Contact Us

It depends on your company size and activity. In general, Emiratisation requirements apply to private-sector companies with 50 or more employees. Smaller companies may not have mandatory quotas but can still be subject to other compliance rules depending on their sector.

Emiratisation targets are reviewed periodically by the UAE government and may be updated annually. New thresholds or sector-specific adjustments can be introduced, so it’s important to stay informed.

Yes. Certain outsourced roles can count toward your Emiratisation requirements, as long as they meet the government’s criteria for eligible employment. Partnering with a compliant outsourcing or EOR provider can help optimize your workforce planning without compromising on regulatory obligations.

Non-compliance can result in significant fines, limitations on new work permits, and possible downgrading of your company’s classification, which increases government fees. Penalties also escalate over time, making early compliance the safest approach.

content:
Leave the Heavy Lifting to Us

Tailored Staff Outsourcing Solutions for Your Company!

We help you manage your workforce, covering talent acquisition, visa processing, and payroll, all while complying with local regulations and international standards.

Approved by

Let’s connect

    I'm interested in

    We are approved by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MOHRE), formerly known as the Ministry of Labor, to operate and provide our services throughout the UAE. With our expertise, your company can focus on its core business while we handle all your outsourcing needs.

    Say Goodbye to Hiring Headaches Outsource with Connect Services

    Since 2016 Connect Resources has been providing Employment Outsourcing, Payroll Outsourcing, HR Outsourcing and Talent Acquisition services in the United Arab Emirates and became a trusted outsourcing partner for a number of global and regional brands.

    Contact Us

    Discover Our Services

    Staff Outsourcing

    Make the most of your visit by utilizing the services we have to offer.

    Payroll Outsourcing

    To all of our clients, we offer a premium payroll outsourcing solution.

    HR Outsourcing

    Make the most of your visit by utilizing the services we have to offer.

    Visa Outsourcing

    Make the most of your visit by utilizing the services we have to offer.

    Speak With Our Experts

    Expand Your Business
    with Confidence

    When you work with us all the following services come standard

    SCHEDULE A CALL

    Staff Outsourcing

    Manage Your Human Capital in an efficient manner with Connect Resources’ Staff Outsourcing. Compliance is the key aspect of our service. By outsourcing your staff to us you can rest assured that their visa and payroll needs are handled by experts. We will manage for your company:

    • Visa and work permit
    • Payroll management including benefits, leaves, overtime, etc
    • Insurance options
    • Agreements, Termination, End of service benefits, etc

    Get in Touch

    Payroll Outsourcing

    We will simplify your HR , payroll and compliance processes limiting the risk of system or human error. Sourcing talents through Connect Resources allows us to place them on our local payroll system enabling you to focus on managing their performance while we handle logistics and compliance. Our established business entities ensure alignment with all relevant regulations.

    • Payroll processing – Connect Resources provides a platform for you to see/check/verify the payrolls of the employees auto-managed by one of our Accounts Managers.
    • Management of Employee’s reimbursement and travel expense
    • WPS payments – We will take care of the full WPS and transfer salary process.

    Get in Touch

    HR Outsourcing

    Entrusting administrative tasks to experts allows you to focus on commercially crucial matters. Using our HR outsourcing service will allow to rest assured that all payments to employees are done on time and in line with local rules.

    • Payroll outsourcing
    • Benefits and compensation management
    • Recruitment (temporary, contracted, permanent staffing)
    • Training and development
    • Tracking employee hours
    • Supervising orientation and training
    • Hiring tasks: receive applications, background checks, interviews, etc.
    • Performance appraisal system

    Get in Touch

    Visa Outsourcing

    Visa outsourcing is a powerful solution in the UAE that helps businesses streamline operations and reduce long-term costs. This service is designed for both types of companies—those with a UAE entity and those without—enabling them to hire and pay employees compliantly.

    Key benefits include:

    • Overcoming visa quota limitations (for local companies)
    • No need to rent a larger office to expand your team (for local companies)
    • Reducing the Emiratisation quota percentage (for local companies)
    • Hiring and paying employees compliantly without a UAE entity (for international companies)

    Get in Touch

    Inspiring Stories from Inspiring Customers

    Artemij Fedosejev

    General Manager, Dubai-based software development company

    We’ve outsourced multiple roles through this company, and every time the process has been smooth. They handled everything—from sourcing staff to managing visas—so we could focus on growing our business. Highly recommend their all-in-one solution!

    Josue Nguinabe

    Operations Head, E-gaming Event Company

    Getting visa quotes and short-term staff used to be a headache—now it’s fast and hassle-free. They even helped us with urgent last-minute cases and delivered every time.

    Luke O’Rouke

    Finance Manager, Tech Startup

    My team used to spend days managing payroll, but since outsourcing it, things are accurate, on time, and fully compliant with UAE regulations. It’s a huge relief knowing it’s all taken care of.

    Lyne Anastassiou Hage

    Global HR Director, Fintech

    Their HR outsourcing support has been a game-changer. No more stressing over labor law compliance or employee documentation. The team is responsive, professional, and understands the UAE market inside out.

    Marc Cirera

    Co-Founder, drop shipping company

    We reduced overhead by outsourcing both our HR and staffing needs. The team helped us find qualified talent quickly, handled onboarding, and provided ongoing support. Great value for money!

    Outsourcing Done Right: The Connect Way

    Choose Connect Resources as your outsourcing partner and experience the benefits of our cost-efficient solutions and unparalleled quality of service. Let us help you achieve your business goals today!

    Contact Us

    Let Our Experts help you find the
    Best Solution in Middle East

    We can guide you through each step of the Staff Outsourcing Solutions – Let’s have a conversation!

    Get more information

title: Freelance Journey
content:
Dreaming of living in Dubai?

Grab your Freelance Residency Today!

Approved by

Your Freelance journey starts here.


    Embrance a World of Benefits

    Step into the world of freelance possibilities and explore the incredible benefits that await you with a Freelance residency in the UAE.

    Realize Your Dreams

    Need financial support to turn your entrepreneurial visions into reality? With a Freelance residency, you can apply for a loan to fuel your business endeavors and unlock your full potential.

    Unlock Full Banking Benefits in the UAE

    With our freelance visa, you can obtain a salary certificate to open a resident bank account in the UAE—giving you access to tax-free income, savings options, and the full range of banking privileges. Whether you’re building your savings or managing day-to-day finances, enjoy seamless banking access just like any UAE resident. Our visa enables you to meet key requirements for opening a bank account and accessing essential financial services.

    Empower Your Loved Ones

    As a holder of a Freelance residency, you enjoy the unique privilege of being able to sponsor your family members. This means you can secure residency for your dependants, allowing them to experience the incredible benefits and joys of living in the UAE right alongside you. By bringing your loved ones to this vibrant country, you not only enhance your own experience but also create lasting memories together.

    Hit the Open Road

    Obtain a UAE driver’s license and embrace the freedom of exploring the UAE’s roads and highways. Embark on exciting road trips, discover hidden gems, and experience the thrill of the open journey.

    Residency-Ready?

title: UAE Silver Visa
content:
Get Your Silver Visa in the UAE

& Enjoy 5 Years Residency

Seamless, fast-track pathway to long-term residency

Extended stay

No local sponsor required

Family inclusivity

Sponsor unlimited domestic visas

At Connect Resources, we offer comprehensive services to help you make the most of your living, business and investment in the UAE.

Book your free consultation

Are you an investor, entrepreneur, or skilled professional looking to thrive in the UAE’s dynamic global economy?

Maybe you are a student with an excellent academic record and want to benefit from the UAE’s exceptional education system. Or, you are perhaps a retiree planning to enjoy your golden years experiencing luxury living in the Emirates.

The UAE Silver Visa can help fulfil your dreams of living, working, or studying in the UAE. The Silver Visa program offers individuals a 5-year residency in the UAE, with the option to renew it.

Why Choose Connect Resources?

Transparent Pricing

Hassle-Free Management

Personalized Assistance

The UAE Silver Visa is a great opportunity for skilled individuals, entrepreneurs, and investors to secure their future in the country. We guide clients at every step of the visa application process with transparency.

Here is what sets Connect Resources apart:

Slide
In-depth understanding

of the local industry, ever-evolving rules and procedures.

Slide
Strong connection

with authorities, which allows for fast application processing.

Slide
Tailored support

to maximise the chance of UAE Silver Visa approval on the first attempt.

Slide
Multilingual support

with advisors fluent in English, Hindi, Arabic and other major languages.

Slide
Transparent and affordable

costs to take the financial burden off Silver Visa applicants.

Slide
Commitment to compliance

with all Silver Visa terms, ensuring long-term approval validity.

Strong connection

Tailored support

Multilingual support

Transparent and affordable

costs to take the financial burden off Silver Visa applicants.

Commitment to compliance

with all Silver Visa terms, ensuring long-term approval validity.

Get Comprehensive Support for the UAE Silver Visa Application

At Connect Resources, we provide comprehensive services and end-to-end support for your UAE Silver Visa application to ensure successful outcomes.

Eligibility assessment

We study your profile and background to determine your eligibility for a Silver Visa based on your goals.

Documentation assistance

From gathering important documents to guiding on attested translations, we ensure all requirements are met.

Filling application form

Our team will fill all forms on your behalf, minimising errors and avoiding clarification requests later during processing.

Application submission

We submit the complete documents via designated authorities, following appropriate procedures.

VISA approval alerts

After submission, we will update you on the status of your application for the UAE Silver Visa.

Get End-to-End Services Beyond Visa processing

At Connect Resources, our team offers full concierge support with:

Emirates ID registration

Medical tests & biometrics

Visa stamping

Dependents’ visa applications

…and more as you need to work, study, live, or open a business in the UAE.

SPEAK TO OUR VISA CONSULTANT TODAY

Why choose us for Dubai Residence Visas?

Slide
Residency visa (Silver visa for entrepreneurs or investors)

Individuals looking to invest in business or property in the UAE. They require a minimum investment of 1 million DHS.

Slide
Retirement visa

For individuals aged 55 or above seeking peaceful retirement years in the UAE. They require a minimum of AED 500,000 in a pension fund or property worth over 1 million DHS in the country.

Slide
Salary-based Silver Visa

Skilled designation visa holders earning above 15,000 AED monthly in the UAE.

Slide
Silver Visa for specialised talent

Professionals with exceptional skills in science, technology, engineering, and healthcare must hold advanced degrees, certifications, or major achievements in their fields.

Slide
Silver Visa for family members

Family members of eligible applicants can be included in the application so they can stay with their loved ones in the UAE.

Slide
Silver Visa for students

High school students with a minimum of 95% grade and university students with a GPA of at least 3.8.

Choose UAE As Your Second Home with a Silver Visa

SPEAK TO OUR EXPERTS

OTHER SOLUTIONS

We also offer

Freelance Visa

Not sure how long you’ll stay in the UAE? Then this is the perfect visa choice for you! Choose a 1- or 2-year option and enjoy all the benefits of residency while you decide if the UAE is right for you. It’s an all-in-one package — visa, work permit, and medical insurance included.

Learn More

Golden Visa

This visa doesn’t just give you the freedom to live and work in the UAE without restrictions — it also makes a bold statement: You made it. You’ve done something amazing. No local sponsor required. No limits on how long you can stay outside the country.

Learn More

Family Visa

Home feels complete with your loved ones by your side — bring your family to the UAE with ease. Whether it’s your spouse, children, or parents, we’ll help you secure residency for them. Already have a UAE visa? Great! If not, we’ve got you covered from start to finish.

Learn More

FAQs

Find answers to the most frequently asked questions about Silver visa in the UAE.

Contact Us

The UAE Silver Visa is a 5-year residency program, while the Golden Visa is a long-term or 10-year residency program.

There is no such thing as “Upgrade your visa”. Instead, your visa is cancelled, and you apply for a new visa.

Yes, eligible Free zone company owners can apply for a Silver Visa. They must fulfill specific requirements, like additional capital investment or job creation.

With expert guidance and support from our consultants, the average time is 7-30 days. However, this varies according to individual cases, additional checks required, and the authority’s workload.

Yes, Silver Visa applicants can simultaneously sponsor their spouses, children, and one executive under the family member category along with the main applicant’s visa process.

Get started with your UAE Silver Visa application

Just fill out the form — we’ll take care of the rest!

Get Tailored Expert Solutions for

All Types of Family Visas in the UAE

Every family is different, and so are their situations and preferences. Our personalized approach ensures all your specific requirements are fulfilled so that you can obtain a family visa faster and successfully.

Spouse Visa

Husband or wife with a valid attested marriage certificate in Arabic or translated into Arabic or English to prove marital relationship. In some cases, a Muslim expatriate may sponsor two wives if they meet certain terms set by the ICP (Federal Authority For Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security).

Child visa

Sponsors holding a 10-year Golden Visa can sponsor unmarried children of any age. Holders of 2-year visas can sponsor unmarried daughters without age restrictions and unmarried sons up to 25 years of age (except for sons with special needs).

Maid visa

Looking to hire domestic help from your home country or any other nation? We can guide you through the visa process, ensuring legal and regulatory compliance.

Parents visa

Sponsor parents for a one-year stay if your minimum salary in the UAE is AED 20,000 with a 2 BHK flat. You need to prove kinship and your ability to take care of them.

Our expert team of immigration experts will guide you through the eligibility criteria, documentation, and application process for each type of family visa in the UAE.

Get Started with
Connect Resources

We are committed to reuniting you and your family or bringing the necessary help to the UAE. We take pride in our proven track record and personalised approach, allowing expedited results. Contact us to get started with a stress-free family visa process in the UAE.

Schedule A Call

Other Services

We also offer

Freelance Visa

Enjoy tax-free income in the UAE! This visa allows you to legally live and work in or from the UAE while enjoying all the benefits of residency—open a bank account, rent a long-term apartment, access UAE medical insurance, and much more.

Learn More

Golden Visa

Enjoy 10 years of residency in the UAE with the Golden Visa—designed for investors and professionals. The Golden Visa gives you the freedom to live in the UAE on your own terms—no local sponsor required, no restrictions, and no limitations on time spent outside the country.

Learn More

Silver Visa

The Silver Visa is a 5-year residency permit—perfect if you’re planning to call the UAE your long-term home. Whether you’re looking to settle down or expand your business, the Silver Visa offers up to 5 years of validity without the need for a local sponsor.

Learn More

FAQs

Find answers to the most frequently asked questions about family visas in the UAE.

Contact Us

The main sponsor must have a valid residency permit and meet minimum salary requirements. They also need to provide necessary documentation. This includes attested marriage and birth certificates.

For sponsoring a spouse or child:

  • Minimum salary requirement is AED 4,000
  • Alternatively, AED 3,000 plus accommodation

For sponsoring parents:

  • Minimum salary requirement is AED 20,000
  • Alternatively, AED 19,000 plus a two-bedroom accommodation

Yes, comprehensive medical insurance is now mandatory for all sponsored family members, including children and parents.

To renew a Family Visa, you’ll need:

  • The sponsor’s residency permit
  • An updated salary certificate
  • Emirates ID
  • Passport copies of family members
  • Proof of continued accommodation

Yes, you can, if you meet the minimum income requirements and other criteria.

  • Maintain clear communication with employees regarding the co-employer relationship, their responsibilities, and rights.

Professional Employer Organization UAE fees vary depending on several factors, including the services offered, the size of your company, and the complexity of your needs. Most PEOs charge a per-employee, per-month (PEPM) fee.

  • Conduct thorough research: Understand your specific needs and requirements.
  • Compare PEOs: Obtain quotes and compare services and pricing from different providers.
  • Check references: Request references from other organizations using the same PEO.
  • Consider experience and expertise: Choose a PEO with experience in your industry, company size, and location.
  • Review the contract: Carefully examine the contract terms and conditions before signing.

content:
UAE Property Visa

Get your investment visa in UAE in just a few steps with us!

Now you can truly call Dubai your own. Property Visa UAE is your gateway to long-term residency in one of the world’s most vibrant cities. Your property becomes more than just a home — it’s your entryway to a future full of possibilities.

Contact Us

ABOUT UAE PROPERTY VISA

Are you wondering about applying for a UAE Property Visa?

A Property Visa in UAE is a residence visa for property investors — without needing a local sponsor. From sleek apartments to lavish villas and off-plan developments, your property investment grants you and your family access to long term residency and a world of opportunities.

Schedule A Call

How It Works

Being eligible for a UAE property visa requires purchasing real estate with title deed value meeting the government’s criteria. Already a property owner? You’re halfway there! Leave the paperwork to us, and we’ll fast-track your Property Visa, getting you settled in no time. And if you’re in a rush, our express service delivers
your visa in as little as a week — so you can start enjoying the UAE lifestyle, stress-free.

Contact Us

Property Visa Criteria

Criteria set by Dubai Land Department to obtain property visa:

For 2-year Property Visa

A property investment of minimum AED 750 thousand

For mortgaged property, 50% should be paid

In the case of a mortgage, AED 1 million of property value should be paid to the bank.

For 10-year Property Visa

Property value of minimum AED 2 million

The total amount can be divided across three properties

You must have the following requirements for obtaining the UAE Property Visa

  • A copy of your passport
  • Title Deed
  • A passport sized photograph
  • Medical insurance

  • A No Objection Certificate proving the amount paid for mortgaged property.

Apply Now

Need Help With Property Visa Application?

Contact our experts for their assistance.

SCHEDULE A CALL

Benefits of Property Visa UAE

As a property investor, you can enjoy the tremendous benefits the UAE Authorities offer to those that invest in the country.

Enjoy unmatched freedom and independence with a Property Visa in Dubai with no need for local sponsorship. Compared to other visas, this one lets you live, invest, and even set up your own company without restrictions, giving you full control over your next big move in the UAE.

You can apply for a driving license in the UAE with ease and explore the country at your own pace. There’s nothing holding you back from visiting the scenic landscapes of the country.

With a property investor visa UAE, you can sponsor your loved ones. Share with them the joys of living together in the UAE

Dubai’s tax-free environment makes your property investment even more lucrative without any additional taxes.

Apply Now

content:
Working remotely abroad for a UK compan

with Connect Resources

More Information

Submit your request


    Working remotely from abroad for a company in the United Kingdom has never been as easy and simple as it is now. For all people who seek to make the most of the benefits of working in European or American countries without being residents, there comes Connect Resources, a leading company in provides help and advice to foreigners, residents, freelancers, investors, and tourists.

    Working remotely from UAE has never been easier

    For people looking for a country from which to work remotely for companies abroad, Connect Resources opens the doors of UAE, where you can not only settle, live and work, but also take full advantage of the benefits that the country offers to workers, benefits such as:

    If you are a tax resident, there are no personal income taxes.

    Dubai is one of the emirates where a wide variety of leisure activities are offered so that remote employees can relax and regain strength.

    Healthcare in Dubai is among the best in the world. However, if you are a temporary resident you must purchase health insurance.

    Wide variety of homes that fit any budget.

    Working remotely from Dubai is very easy and does not need to be set up by the company.

    If you are a tax resident, there are no personal income taxes.

    The gross salary in Dubai is equal to the net salary.

    You can get a much better lifestyle than in most countries in the world. Plus, you can enjoy a unique culture that you can experience while working remotely for a company anywhere in the world.

    For all of the above to be a reality, you must have an ally in the country to help you obtain a visa, permits, advice, and documentation.

    Contact us now and
    connect with the opportunities that UAE offers for you

    CONTACT US NOW

    FAQs

    Still have questions? We will be happy to answer them.

    Contact Us

    You can work remotely for countries like The United Kingdom, Spain, Germany, Portugal, Iceland, and many others.

    The documents you need to enter the UAE are the ones you will see below:

    • Passport with a minimum expiration date of 6 after entering the United Arab Emirates.
    • Initially, you need a tourist visa to enter the country, and while there you have three months to obtain a valid work permit from the Ministry of Labor.
    • Medical certificates that must be endorsed by the relevant authorities in the UAE.
    • Sponsor of Connect Resources to help you with all the paperwork and advise you in the process.

    Working remotely in the UAE offers many benefits for both employees and UK businesses themselves. Among those benefits you can find:

    • The UK has very important companies that can provide many benefits to foreign employees.
    • Globally competitive salaries.
    • It reduces stress and can increase the productivity of the employee and the company itself.
    • Qualified people can aspire to a good job, even if they are foreigners.
    • You can expect to receive the same salary as employees who are UK residents, even working remotely enjoying the benefits offered by the great nation that is the UAE.

    There is no possible disadvantage, especially if you have the advice of a Connect Resources agent.

content:
Payroll Outsourcing UAE 

We Handle Payroll While You Can Focus on Core Tasks of Your Business.

A seamless and cost-effective solution enabling companies to manage employee payroll accurately, without the need to invest in or maintain an in-house system.

Get a Free Consultation

Reach out to us and let our experts guide you toward success!

    I'm interested in

    What is Payroll Outsourcing?

    About Payroll outsourcing 

    Outsourcing your payroll in the UAE means that a third-party organization will handle the entire payroll process for your business. A payroll outsourcing company will manage your employees’ pay-slips, bonuses, deductions, and reimbursements, including the Wage Protection System (WPS) process. They ensure your data is secure against unauthorized access and minimize the risk of errors.

    Payroll outsourcing companies specialize in resolving any obstacles your business may face regarding employee payroll. Given the diverse workforce in the UAE, payroll outsourcing service providers in Dubai often offer expertise in handling payroll matters for expatriate employees, including compliance with visa and residency regulations, tax implications, and currency conversions.

    Schedule A Call

    Our Payroll outsourcing process

    As a service provider we ensure everything is according to the UAE laws and regulations but the plus side of payroll outsourcing services in Dubai is that we prioritize confidentiality and security of your payroll data in accordance with data protection laws.

    We administrate your employee salaries, wages, bonuses, incentives, and benefits based on your employee time sheets and attendance records. Calculating and making error free deductions. Offer you a customized solution that fits your business.

Know more

Connect Resources supplies Employers of Record services to customers that require employing personnel and managing payroll without making a branch office or subsidiary in Libya. You can to collaborate with our PEO in Libya. This to keep in line with local labor laws within a few days.

Our EOR solution allows customers to manage payroll in Libya while we are in charge of HR services, taxes, and compliance management. We are able to provide the most suitable employment contract practices, statutory and customary benefits, and employee expenses, as well as severance and termination if necessary.

Libya is a developing nation that is quickly taking strides in the digital and business world. The country is a great place to find talent for any organization. As it offers a wide range of highly skilled and motivated individuals that can help a company reach its goals. Companies in Libya are also able to benefit from the country’s very low cost of living which makes it very attractive for employers.

Hiring in Libya

Employment contracts in Libya are under the Labour Law of 1977. This law sets out the rights and obligations of employers and employees in the country. It includes provisions related to minimum wages, working hours, holidays, overtime, termination of contracts, and other related matters. Furthermore, the law also sets forth the procedures for the formation of an employment agreement between the employer and the employee.

Working Hours in Libya

The average working hours in Libya vary depending on the sector and the job. Generally, the normal working hours in Libya range from 8 to 10 hours per day, with a maximum of 12 hours per day. The standard working week is 48 hours, with a maximum of 60 hours per week. Overtime is common, but only after authorization from the Ministry of Labor. Workers have the right to one day off each week, usually on Fridays.

Holidays in Libya

  • February 17th Revolution
  • Labour Day
  • Eid al-Fitr
  • Arafat Day
  • Eid Al-Adha
  • Hijri New Year
  • Martyrs’ Day
  • Liberation Day
  • Birthday of Prophet Muhammed
  • Independence Day

Vacation Days in Libya

Annual leave in Libya is an important part of the country’s labor policies. Employees have a right to a minimum of 20 working days of paid leave per year. And this may extend depending on the individual’s contract and position.

During this time, employees are free to use their leave as they wish, such as for vacation, religious holidays, or to take care of personal matters.

There are also special provisions for employees who are injured or become ill while on the job. Thus, allowing them to take additional leave days without penalty.

Sick Leave in Libya

  • Employees can take up to three months of sick leave each year, if they have a doctor’s certificate.
  • During their sick leave, employers have to pay for the employee’s medical expenses, as well as providing at least 50% of the employee’s salary.
  • Employees who are sick for more than three months will receive a minimum pension from the government.

Parental Leave in Libya

  • Mothers have a right to three months of maternity leave at full pay.
  • This leave can extend to six months under certain circumstances.
  • Additionally, mothers have access to an additional two months of leave without pay.

Supplementary Benefits in Libya

The labor law in Libya requires all employers to provide health insurance coverage for their employees. This coverage must include protection against illness and injury, as well as access to medical care. Employers also have to pay for any medical expenses associating with the employee’s illness or injury. Employees have a right to receive a percentage of their wages in the event of an illness or injury that prevents them from working. Additionally, employers must provide coverage for any medical emergencies while the employee is on the job.

Health Insurance in Libya

Libya offers a range of supplementary benefits to its citizens. These include medical and health benefits, educational benefits, housing and infrastructure benefits, and subsidies for food and fuel.

Termination Process in Libya

Employment termination in Libya is legally governed by the Libyan Labour Law No. (17) of 2010. This law stipulates that employees must receive with fair and reasonable notice prior to termination, and that employers must pay any unpaid wages and benefits within 15 days of termination.

Furthermore, employers may not terminate employees in cases of pregnancy, maternity leave, or any other case relating to the employee’s gender. And must provide a written notice and payment of compensation in the event of termination.

Therefore, employers in Libya must comply with the legal requirements when terminating employees.

Taxes in Libya

In Libya, employees are subject to income tax, which is calculated based on their total income. The income tax rate is 10% on the total income earned for the year. With an additional 5% for income earned above a certain threshold.

Employees also have to pay social security contributions, which makes up 7% of their total income. Tax declarations must go to the relevant authorities before the end of the fiscal year. As a result, this can be done online or in person at a tax office.

Our Services
Contact Us

Expand where you want to be!

Guiding your Growth Beyond Borders

We Help You Expand

Confidently hire employees and contractors while staying squeaky clean on the compliance front – all without the fuss of setting up a local entity.

We Hire & Onboard

Say goodbye to hiring headaches and hello to a top-notch talent strategy. Elevate your compensation game with tailor-made perks. Outsource your staff to us, and we’ll handle visas, payroll, and all the nitty-gritty details.

We Manage Payroll

We’ve got the full spectrum covered—HR, payroll, compliance, and more. We manage the timesheets, and we ensure every paycheck complies with UAE’s WPS regulations.

Our Leadership

From Vision to Victory

Learn more about our journey from our leadership

“Connect Resources was not built in a day. Year after year, we’ve remained committed to something deeper than mere change – we’re here to create substantial impact on businesses within and beyond the GCC.
We’re here to help with HR in the new world where people can work from anywhere. We make things easier by handling local payroll, employment, and international hiring, and we offer great benefits for employees and contractors. Our journey has been a big success, and now Connect Resources is a group of over 25 companies. We help customers with everything, from starting a business in Dubai to growing across the Middle East. It can be tough to figure out how to expand in the Middle East, especially if you don’t have a local office, but at Connect Resources, we’re here to make it simpler and ensure your growth in the UAE.”

title: Contingent Staffing
content:

Contingent Staffing Service Dubai, UAE

Add temporary employees to your staff with our contingent staffing services. With us, you will be able to hire workers for particular projects. Let professionals handle your recruitment process in the region.

    [vc_custom_heading text=”Let Our Experts help you find the Best Solution in Middle East” font_container=”tag:h3|text_align:left” use_theme_fonts=”yes” css=”%7B%22default%22%3A%7B%22color%22%3A%22%231a1a1a%22%2C%22font-size%22%3A%2240px%22%2C%22font-family%22%3A%22body%22%2C%22font-weight%22%3A%22500%22%7D%7D”]
    Schedule a Call

    What is Contingent staffing in Dubai

    Contingent staffing is collection of individuals working for the company on a project-by-project basis. This workforce is typically comprised of consultants, temporary employees, freelancers, independent contractors, etc. who operate under a contract. These employees do not work for the company full-time. The culture of contingent labor is expanding because it offers greater flexibility and because businesses are having trouble filling unfilled positions with qualified candidates.

    With contingent staffing Dubai, support businesses will be able to delegate the hiring and recruitment process to professionals. In this way, they can obtain expert support with finding, interviewing, and hiring workers.

    Contact Us

    Our Services

    EOR

    PEO

    Payroll Outsourcing

    Staff Outsourcing

    Visa Outsourcing

    Recruitment Services

    How it works

Qatar – Employer of Record

Expand your Business in Qatar

Get started today

Know more

For clients who want to hire staff members and manage payroll without initially setting up a subsidiary or branch in Qatar, our business offers employer of record services. With our Qatar PEO, your applicant is employed in accordance with regional labor rules and can be onboarded as quickly as possible. Connect Resources will carry out your in-country needs as liable as possible.

Customers can handle payroll in Qatar with our all-inclusive solution and PEO service while we take care of their HR services, tax obligations, and compliance management needs. As a EOR/PEO expert, we handle employee expenses, benefits, best practices for employment contracts, and termination when necessary. Also, we update you on any modifications to Qatar’s local employment legislation.

Hiring in Qatar

Qatar’s visa sponsorship program: Foreigners make up almost 90% of Qatar’s workforce. As a result, our clients require our services to both place a worker on a regional payroll and sponsor the person’s work permit for Qatar. This is a typical aspect of our provider and is typically attainable. Before we can determine whether our local firm can sponsor the visa, in some circumstances, the citizenship or work history of an individual may need to be checked.

We advise being clear about whether the company would solely sponsor the employee’s employment and residency permits or whether it will also sponsor the candidate’s family members’ residency permits when discussing with a candidate in Qatar. It’s typical for employers of professionals to sponsor the spouse’s and children’s residency visas.

Employment Contracts in Qatar

In Qatar, it is necessary to have an employment agreement in place that specifies the conditions of the employee’s pay, perks, and termination obligations. Additionally, the salary and any other remuneration amounts should always be in local rather than foreign currency in an employment contract in Qatar.

Working Hours in Qatar

According to the local labor law, employees must work 8 hours a day and 48 hours a week maximum. Nevertheless, during Ramadan this lows to 6 hours a day and 36 hours a week.

Holidays in Qatar

There are 8 national holidays in the region.

Vacation Days in Qatar

Statutory Minimum: After one year of continuous service, an employee is eligible for the following yearly leave with pay:

  • 3 weeks of paid leave after between one and five years of service.
  • 4 weeks of paid time off after five years of service.

During partial years of service, this is prorated. Before the employee takes his annual leave, the company must pay him. This includes the vacation pay to which the worker has a right to; also this will include the amount to which the worker qualifies for, for the work that they have completed up until the time of taking the leave.

In Qatar, the standard market vacation allotment for executives is frequently expanded to 4 weeks of paid leave.

Also, firms offer a yearly round-trip ticket to the worker’s home nation during the vacation period. We advise making it clear to employees whether they will receive the yearly round-trip ticket for their complete family or just themselves.

Moreover, Muslim employees may take up to two weeks of unpaid time off for religious purposes during the course of their employment.

Sick Leave in Qatar

After working for three months, Qatari employees are eligible for sick leave pay. Therefore, workers can take up to two weeks. As a result, to be eligible for this benefit, you must submit a medical certificate.

Parental Leave in Qatar

If a woman has been working for the firm for a full year, she is eligible for 50 days of maternity leave. Consequently, they can take up to two weeks before birth and at least a month after.

Although there is no legal paternity leave, many employers do provide fathers with between three and five days of leave pay.

Health Insurance in Qatar

Healthcare for Qataris is either totally free or quite cheap. In general, expats want additional insurance.}

Supplementary Benefits in Qatar

Employee benefits in Qatar frequently include additional health and life insurance. We advise being up front about whether life and health insurance coverage will be given to the employee solely or to the employee’s family when negotiating with candidates. As part of our service, Connect Resources will set up insurance benefits for the worker when they sign up for our employee outsourcing scheme.

Salary, housing benefits, and transport allowance typically make up total pay in Qatar. Some workers in Qatar may also bargain for educational benefits for their kids. Generally speaking, we advise negotiating the entire remuneration package. The local contract of employment may divide the agreed-upon total remuneration into smaller sums to reflect any necessary allowances once the annual pay has been agreed upon.

In Qatar, additional allowances and bonuses are frequently negotiated, and depending on the structure, they may or may not be taxable. Connect Resources provides comprehensive pay package advice to clients using our Employer of Record service at every stage of the process.

Termination in Qatar

Six months is the maximum probationary period. A worker may only undergo one probationary period with a single employer. The company may terminate the agreement within the probationary period with 3 days’ notice; this, if the employer considers the worker is unable to perform job tasks.

In Qatar, end-of-service rewards are due to any employee who has worked for an organization for more than a year. The remuneration due consists of the base salary plus any applicable cost-of-living adjustments, as well as:

  • Up to five years of continuous service, 3 weeks are granted for every year of service.
  • The second five years of continuous employment are worth four weeks for every year of service.
  • Over the following ten years of service, there will be 5 weeks for every year of service.
  • 6 weeks are added to every year of service that exceeds 20 years of nonstop employment.

The employee must pay this amount within seven days of their last day of employment with the company. In reality, most businesses pay an amount for each full or partial year of employment that is equal to one month’s wage.

Employees with indefinite contracts often have a 30-day notice period if they have been with the company for less than five years. The notification period is at least 2 months before the date of termination; this, if the length of service exceeds five years.

Employers who sponsor work visas and residency permits pay for the employee’s departure to their home country. Also, they are responsible for making sure they depart within seven days of receiving their exit permit. The employer may notify the police or migration authorities if this 7-day window is overrun.

Taxes in Qatar

There are no individual social security taxes or personal income taxes.

Why choose us?

It takes time, money, and complexity to set up a subsidiary in Qatar to employ a small workforce. Strong worker safeguards are provided by Qatari labor legislation. Which calls for careful review of every detail and familiarity with regional best practices.

Qatar expansion is simple and quick with Connect Resources. Without having to deal with the hassle of establishing a foreign branch office, we can assist you in hiring the candidate of your choice, deal with HR issues and payroll, and make sure you are in compliance with local laws. Our EOR and Qatar PEO solution gives you peace of mind so you can concentrate on managing your business.

Connect Resources will carry out your in-country needs as liable as possible.

Customers can handle payroll in Qatar with our all-inclusive solution and PEO service while we take care of their HR services, tax obligations, and compliance management needs. As a EOR/PEO expert, we handle employee expenses, benefits, best practices for employment contracts, and termination when necessary. Also, we update you on any modifications to Qatar’s local employment legislation.

Hiring in Qatar

Qatar’s visa sponsorship program: Foreigners make up almost 90% of Qatar’s workforce. As a result, our clients require our services to both place a worker on a regional payroll and sponsor the person’s work permit for Qatar. This is a typical aspect of our provider and is typically attainable. Before we can determine whether our local firm can sponsor the visa, in some circumstances, the citizenship or work history of an individual may need to be checked.

We advise being clear about whether the company would solely sponsor the employee’s employment and residency permits or whether it will also sponsor the candidate’s family members’ residency permits when discussing with a candidate in Qatar. It’s typical for employers of professionals to sponsor the spouse’s and children’s residency visas.

Employment Contracts in Qatar

In Qatar, it is necessary to have an employment agreement in place that specifies the conditions of the employee’s pay, perks, and termination obligations. Additionally, the salary and any other remuneration amounts should always be in local rather than foreign currency in an employment contract in Qatar.

Working Hours in Qatar

According to the local labor law, employees must work 8 hours a day and 48 hours a week maximum. Nevertheless, during Ramadan this lows to 6 hours a day and 36 hours a week.

Holidays in Qatar

There are 8 national holidays in the region.

Vacation Days in Qatar

Statutory Minimum: After one year of continuous service, an employee is eligible for the following yearly leave with pay:

  • 3 weeks of paid leave after between one and five years of service.
  • 4 weeks of paid time off after five years of service.

During partial years of service, this is prorated. Before the employee takes his annual leave, the company must pay him. This includes the vacation pay to which the worker has a right to; also this will include the amount to which the worker qualifies for, for the work that they have completed up until the time of taking the leave.

In Qatar, the standard market vacation allotment for executives is frequently expanded to 4 weeks of paid leave.

Also, firms offer a yearly round-trip ticket to the worker’s home nation during the vacation period. We advise making it clear to employees whether they will receive the yearly round-trip ticket for their complete family or just themselves.

Moreover, Muslim employees may take up to two weeks of unpaid time off for religious purposes during the course of their employment.

Sick Leave in Qatar

After working for three months, Qatari employees are eligible for sick leave pay. Therefore, workers can take up to two weeks. As a result, to be eligible for this benefit, you must submit a medical certificate.

Parental Leave in Qatar

If a woman has been working for the firm for a full year, she is eligible for 50 days of maternity leave. Consequently, they can take up to two weeks before birth and at least a month after.

Although there is no legal paternity leave, many employers do provide fathers with between three and five days of leave pay.

Health Insurance in Qatar

Healthcare for Qataris is either totally free or quite cheap. In general, expats want additional insurance.}

Supplementary Benefits in Qatar

Employee benefits in Qatar frequently include additional health and life insurance. We advise being up front about whether life and health insurance coverage will be given to the employee solely or to the employee’s family when negotiating with candidates. As part of our service, Connect Resources will set up insurance benefits for the worker when they sign up for our employee outsourcing scheme.

Salary, housing benefits, and transport allowance typically make up total pay in Qatar. Some workers in Qatar may also bargain for educational benefits for their kids. Generally speaking, we advise negotiating the entire remuneration package. The local contract of employment may divide the agreed-upon total remuneration into smaller sums to reflect any necessary allowances once the annual pay has been agreed upon.

In Qatar, additional allowances and bonuses are frequently negotiated, and depending on the structure, they may or may not be taxable. Connect Resources provides comprehensive pay package advice to clients using our Employer of Record service at every stage of the process.

Termination in Qatar

Six months is the maximum probationary period. A worker may only undergo one probationary period with a single employer. The company may terminate the agreement within the probationary period with 3 days’ notice; this, if the employer considers the worker is unable to perform job tasks.

In Qatar, end-of-service rewards are due to any employee who has worked for an organization for more than a year. The remuneration due consists of the base salary plus any applicable cost-of-living adjustments, as well as:

  • Up to five years of continuous service, 3 weeks are granted for every year of service.
  • The second five years of continuous employment are worth four weeks for every year of service.
  • Over the following ten years of service, there will be 5 weeks for every year of service.
  • 6 weeks are added to every year of service that exceeds 20 years of nonstop employment.

The employee must pay this amount within seven days of their last day of employment with the company. In reality, most businesses pay an amount for each full or partial year of employment that is equal to one month’s wage.

Employees with indefinite contracts often have a 30-day notice period if they have been with the company for less than five years. The notification period is at least 2 months before the date of termination; this, if the length of service exceeds five years.

Employers who sponsor work visas and residency permits pay for the employee’s departure to their home country. Also, they are responsible for making sure they depart within seven days of receiving their exit permit. The employer may notify the police or migration authorities if this 7-day window is overrun.

Taxes in Qatar

There are no individual social security taxes or personal income taxes.

Qatar expansion is simple and quick with Connect Resources.
